query: How do I get a red wine stain out of a carpet?
answer:
Work fast and don't rub, because rubbing spreads the wine and pushes it deeper into the fibers. Blot up as much as you can with a clean white cloth, working from the edge of the stain inward, and add a little cold water as you go. Never use hot water, because heat can set the stain [1][2].

Next, mix about one tablespoon of dish soap and one tablespoon of white vinegar into two cups of cold water. Sponge it onto the stain, let it sit for a few minutes, and keep blotting until no more color comes up [3].

If some color is still there, mix two parts 3% hydrogen peroxide with one part dish soap and apply it [2]. Peroxide works like a mild bleach, so test it on a hidden patch first, especially on colored or wool carpet [3]. When you're done, rinse the area with cold water, blot it dry, and vacuum once it's fully dry. If the stain is old or still won't come out, try an enzyme or oxygen-based carpet cleaner, or call a professional.
